mainTopic: Does our משנה follow רבי ישמעאל, with lashes even for an oath broken without action? And how does that fit with רבי יוחנן's rulings?
overview: The גמרא wants to fit our משנה with רבי ישמעאל, who holds that a קרבן is brought only for oaths about the future. It first objects that the משנה lists its four oath cases just like the four shades of נגעים, so all four must carry liability. The answer is that past oaths bring מלקות instead of a קרבן, based on רבא's teaching that the Torah links a שבועת שקר to a שבועת שוא. Then the גמרא asks how 'I will eat' and not eating can bring lashes, since nothing was done. It answers that רבי ישמעאל gives lashes even for a לאו שאין בו מעשה. This creates a contradiction in רבי יוחנן's rulings. He says the הלכה follows an unnamed משנה, yet in the loaf case he rules that a לאו שאין בו מעשה brings no lashes. The גמרא answers that he followed a different unnamed משנה. A suggestion from פסחים is rejected, because it may follow רבי יהודה's separate reason. The גמרא then begins citing the real source, the משנה about swearing twice not to eat a loaf, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The comparison to leprous marks shows all four cases are liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that only some of the four oath cases carry liability. It points out that the משנה lists them just like the four shades of נגעים, which all count.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה lists these cases just like the shades of leprous marks! Just as there, all four shades bring liability, so here too, all four cases should bring liability!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion that some of the four oath cases in the משנה bring no liability at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses the same pattern ('two that are four') for oaths and for מראות נגעים. With נגעים, all four shades make a person טמא, so none of them are 'empty' cases. So the four oath cases should likewise all be cases of liability.

keyTerms.meaning: similar to, in the same pattern as

phrases.english: But it teaches them similar to the shades of leprous marks –
phrases.notes: The opening משנה of the מסכת lists oaths and the shades of נגעים in the same 'two that are four' pattern.

phrases.english: just as there, all of them are for liability,
so too here, all of them are for liability!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the earlier suggestion that the משנה's four cases include both liable and exempt cases.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that only some of the four oath cases bring liability.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The parallel structure with מראות נגעים, where all four shades count, shows that all four oath cases must also be cases of liability.

steps.title: It is רבי ישמעאל: past oaths bring lashes, not a קרבן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה really is רבי ישמעאל. He exempts past oaths only from a קרבן, but still holds that they bring מלקות. So all four cases carry some liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the משנה follows רבי ישמעאל. And when רבי ישמעאל says one is not liable for past oaths, he means not liable for a קרבן. But he does hold that one gets lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps רבי ישמעאל as the author of the משנה, and explains that 'liability' for past oaths means lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that if רבי ישמעאל exempts past oaths from a קרבן, those cases carry no liability at all. The answer splits the two kinds of punishment: no קרבן, but yes מלקות. Now all four cases are 'for liability,' just like נגעים.

keyTerms.meaning: sacrifice (here, the קרבן עולה ויורד for oaths)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי ישמעאל holds past oaths are fine. He only says they don't bring a קרבן. They are still forbidden and bring מלקות.

phrases.english: Actually, it is Rabbi Yishmael;

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי לָא מְחַיֵּיב רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל לְשֶׁעָבַר – קׇרְבָּן;
phrases.english: and when Rabbi Yishmael does not hold one liable for the past – that is for an offering;
but for lashes he certainly holds one liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 while keeping רבי ישמעאל as the author.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between two kinds of liability (קרבן vs. מלקות).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ישמעאל's exemption of past oaths means they carry no liability at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Past oaths are exempt only from a קרבן but bring מלקות, so all four cases are liable.

steps.title: רבא's source: a false oath about the past is like a vain oath
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the claim that past oaths bring lashes with רבא's teaching. The Torah compares שבועת שקר to שבועת שוא. Since שבועת שוא is about the past, שבועת שקר about the past also brings lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows רבא, who said: The Torah clearly included a false oath along with a vain oath. Just as a vain oath is about the past, a false oath is also about the past.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבא's teaching as the source for saying that a false oath about the past is punished with lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שבועת שוא, like swearing that something obvious is false, is about the past and is punished with מלקות. רבא says the Torah put שבועת שקר in the same category. So a false oath about the past also gets מלקות, which backs up the answer in step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: a vain oath (pointless or obviously false)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source that lets past oaths carry real punishment even according to רבי ישמעאל, and it sets up the next question about which cases bring מלקות.

phrases.english: And this is like Rava – for Rava said:
The Torah explicitly included a false oath
to be similar to a vain oath;
just as a vain oath is about the past,
so too a false oath is also about the past.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for step 2's claim that past oaths bring מלקות.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that a false oath about the past brings מלקות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's teaching that the Torah compares שבועת שקר to שבועת שוא, which is about the past.

steps.title: How can 'I will eat' and not eating bring lashes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that three of the four cases bring lashes: the two past oaths by רבא's rule, and 'I will not eat' then eating because an action was done. But 'I will eat' and then not eating involves no action, so why lashes?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for 'I ate' and 'I did not eat', because of רבא. 'I will not eat' and then he ate also works, since it is a prohibition broken by an action. But 'I will eat' and he did not eat, why lashes? It is a prohibition broken without any action!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the new answer case by case. It finds a problem with the fourth case, where the person simply did nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally there are no מלקות for a לאו שאין בו מעשה, a prohibition broken by doing nothing. Saying 'I will eat' and then not eating is broken by sitting still. So the claim that all four cases bring lashes seems to fail for this case.

keyTerms.meaning: a prohibition broken through an action
a prohibition broken without any action, which normally brings no lashes

steps.confusionAlert: The problem here is not about past versus future. 'I will eat' is a future oath. The problem is only that breaking it involves no action, and lashes usually need an action.

phrases.english: Granted 'I ate' and 'I did not eat' – that is like Rava;
'That I will not eat' and he ate, also –
it is a prohibition that involves an action;
but 'I will eat' and he did not eat – why?
it is a prohibition that does not involve an action!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests step 2's claim that all four cases bring מלקות, and finds a problem with one case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that all four oath cases bring מלקות according to רבי ישמעאל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'I will eat' and not eating is a לאו שאין בו מעשה, which normally brings no מלקות. So not all four cases can be liable for lashes.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל gives lashes even without an action
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the question from Step 4: רבי ישמעאל holds that one gets מלקות even for a לאו שאין בו מעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל holds that a person gets lashes even for breaking a prohibition without doing any action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of why 'I will eat' and then not eating brings lashes. It says that רבי ישמעאל holds that lashes apply even when no action was done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most opinions hold that lashes need a physical act of sinning. רבי ישמעאל disagrees and gives lashes even for a sin of doing nothing. That explains how all four oath cases in the משנה can carry lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition broken without any physical action

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael holds:
a prohibition that has no action in it,
one gets lashes for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 4 about the case where no action was done.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes a minority principle to the תנא of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Lashes require an action, so 'I will eat' and not eating cannot bring lashes.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי ישמעאל holds that even a לאו שאין בו מעשה brings lashes, so all four cases carry lashes.

steps.title: A contradiction within רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: If our משנה follows רבי ישמעאל's view, two statements of רבי יוחנן seem to clash.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, there is a contradiction between one statement of רבי יוחנן and another statement of רבי יוחנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge that comes from the answer it just gave. The next two steps bring the two statements of רבי יוחנן that seem to clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer made our unnamed משנה follow רבי ישמעאל, who gives lashes without an action. This step only announces the problem. The sources that prove it come next.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a contradiction between one statement and another

phrases.english: If so,
there is a contradiction between Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Yochanan!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, קַשְׁיָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אַדְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of Step 5 as the starting point for a new challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of רבי יוחנן's rulings once our משנה is said to follow רבי ישמעאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two rulings of רבי יוחנן, put together with Step 5, give opposite results about lashes for an oath broken without an action.

steps.title: First source: the הלכה follows an unnamed משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that the halacha follows a סתם משנה. Our משנה is unnamed, so he should rule like it.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי יוחנן said: The הלכה follows an unnamed משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the first side of the contradiction. רבי יוחנן's general rule is that the halacha follows a משנה that does not name its author.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה names no author, and Step 5 said it follows רבי ישמעאל. So by רבי יוחנן's rule, the הלכה should be that a person gets lashes even without an action.

keyTerms.meaning: A משנה stated without naming any author

phrases.english: For Rabbi Yochanan said:
the halacha follows an unnamed Mishnah;

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הֲלָכָה כִּסְתַם מִשְׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first half of the contradiction announced in Step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן should hold that lashes apply without an action
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's rule that the halacha follows a סתם משנה

steps.title: Second source: רבי יוחנן says no lashes when nothing was done
steps.stepSummary: Someone swore to eat a loaf today and did not eat it. רבי יוחנן says he gets no lashes because no action was done.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: 'I swear I will eat this loaf today,' and the day passed and he did not eat it. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש both say he is not lashed. רבי יוחנן says he is not lashed because it is a prohibition without an action, and one never gets lashes for a prohibition without an action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the second side of the contradiction. In this exact case, רבי יוחנן rules that there are no lashes because nothing was done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי יוחנן clearly holds that a לאו שאין בו מעשה brings no lashes. That is the opposite of רבי ישמעאל's view. Yet רבי יוחנן's own rule says to follow the unnamed משנה, which Step 5 said follows רבי ישמעאל. That is the contradiction.
steps.confusionAlert: Both רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש agree that there are no lashes here. They argue only about the reason. Only רבי יוחנן's reason, that nothing was done, creates the contradiction.

phrases.english: And it was stated:
'I swear that I will eat this loaf today,'
and the day passed and he did not eat it:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish both say:
He is not lashed.
Rabbi Yochanan says he is not lashed

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה לָאו שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה,
phrases.english: because it is a prohibition with no action,
and for any prohibition with no action
one does not get lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִתְּמַר: שְׁבוּעָה שֶׁאוֹכַל כִּכָּר זוֹ הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second half of the contradiction, which clashes with Step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן holds there are no lashes for a לאו שאין בו מעשה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The recorded dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about the loaf oath

steps.title: ריש לקיש's different reason: an uncertain warning
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש also says there are no lashes, but because the warning was uncertain. An uncertain warning does not count as a warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש says he is not lashed because it is an uncertain warning, and an uncertain warning is not called a warning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the dispute with ריש לקיש's reason. His reason has nothing to do with whether an action was done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lashes require a warning (התראה) before the sin. Here, as long as the day is not over, he could still eat the loaf, so any warning is uncertain. ריש לקיש holds such a warning does not count. This reason does not depend on the no-action rule, so the contradiction rests only on רבי יוחנן's reason.

keyTerms.meaning: A warning given before a sin, needed for lashes
A warning given when it is not yet certain that a sin will happen
It is not considered a warning

steps.whatToRemember: The contradiction in רבי יוחנן: he follows an unnamed משנה, and our משנה (as רבי ישמעאל) gives lashes without an action. Yet he himself rules that a לאו שאין בו מעשה brings no lashes. ריש לקיש agrees there are no lashes in the loaf case, but only because the warning was uncertain.

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish says he is not lashed
because it is an uncertain warning,
phrases.notes: Until the day ends, he could still eat the loaf. So no one can warn him for sure that he is about to sin.

phrases.english: and an uncertain warning is not called a warning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quoted dispute from Step 8 by giving ריש לקיש's separate reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An uncertain warning is not a valid warning, so there are no lashes in the loaf case.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן relied on a different unnamed משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the clash: רבי יוחנן found another סתם משנה that holds there are no lashes for a לאו שאין בו מעשה, and he followed that one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן found a different unnamed משנה, and he followed it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from Step 6. רבי יוחנן did follow a סתם משנה, just a different one from ours.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה seems to follow רבי ישמעאל, who gives lashes even without an action. But if there is another סתם משנה that gives no lashes for a לאו שאין בו מעשה, then רבי יוחנן's ruling about the loaf still fits his rule of following a סתם משנה. When two unnamed משניות disagree, he can only follow one of them.

keyTerms.meaning: An unnamed משנה, stated without naming who said it

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan found another unnamed Mishnah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 6 between Steps 7 and 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a competing source: a different סתם משנה that רבי יוחנן followed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's rule of following a סתם משנה should make him rule like our משנה, which follows רבי ישמעאל.
steps.terutzMaskana: Another סתם משנה holds that there are no lashes without an action, and רבי יוחנן followed that one.

steps.title: Which unnamed משנה? A suggestion: leftover meat and broken bones of the קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which other סתם משנה is meant and suggests the משנה in פסחים: one who leaves over meat of a pure קרבן פסח, or breaks a bone of an impure one, does not get the forty lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which unnamed משנה? Suppose it is this one, as we learned: one who leaves over meat of a pure קרבן פסח, and one who breaks a bone of an impure one, does not get the forty lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wants to know which משנה רבי יוחנן found. It offers a candidate, and this sets up the next step, which explains why that משנה would fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The candidate משנה rules that two people do not get מלקות. The word 'אילימא' (if you say) signals that the גמרא is testing this suggestion. Step 13 ends up rejecting it.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say, used to bring up a suggestion that is often rejected
One who leaves over (meat past the time it may be eaten)
The forty lashes, meaning standard מלקות

phrases.english: Which unnamed Mishnah?
If you say it is this unnamed Mishnah, as we learned:
But one who leaves over meat of a pure Pesach offering
and one who breaks a bone of an impure one
does not receive the forty lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the identity of the source mentioned in Step 10 and suggests one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which סתם משנה holds that there are no lashes for a לאו שאין בו מעשה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: First suggestion: the משנה about leaving over meat of a pure קרבן פסח. Step 13 rejects it, and Step 15 gives the real answer: the משנה in שבועות about swearing twice not to eat a loaf.

steps.title: Why the leftover case shows no lashes without an action
steps.stepSummary: The broken bone of an impure פסח is exempt because the פסוק speaks only of a valid offering. Leaving over meat of a pure פסח has no such reason, so the reason must be that it is a לאו שאין בו מעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The broken bone makes sense, because it says 'And you shall not break a bone in it,' which means a valid offering and not a disqualified one. But for leaving over meat of a pure offering, what is the reason there are no lashes? It must be that this is a לאו with no action, and there are no lashes for any לאו with no action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how this משנה supports רבי יוחנן. It sets aside the broken bone case and focuses on the leftover meat case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The broken bone case has its own reason: the word 'בו' limits the איסור to a כשר offering. The leftover case has no special reason, and leaving over meat means doing nothing. So the גמרא suggests the משנה holds there are no lashes for a לאו שאין בו מעשה.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition broken without doing any action

phrases.english: It makes sense regarding one who breaks a bone of an impure one,
as it is written: "And you shall not break a bone in it"
phrases.notes: שמות 12:46. The word 'בו' (in it) is the key.

phrases.english: in a valid one, and not in a disqualified one.
But one who leaves over meat of a pure one, what is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵי לָאו שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה,
phrases.english: Is it not because it is a prohibition that involves no action,
phrases.notes: The first 'לאו' means 'is it not'. The second 'לאו' means 'a prohibition'.

phrases.english: and for any prohibition that involves no action
one does not receive lashes?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the משנה suggested in Step 11 supports רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.raayaObject: That a סתם משנה holds there are no lashes for a לאו שאין בו מעשה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה exempting one who leaves over meat of a pure קרבן פסח from lashes.

steps.title: Maybe that משנה follows רבי יהודה for a different reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the משנה might follow רבי יהודה, who gives no lashes here only because the פסוק puts an עשה (burning the leftovers) right after the לאו. Without that, he would give lashes even with no action.
steps.simpleTranslation: But how do you know this משנה follows רבי יעקב, who says there are no lashes for a לאו with no action? Maybe it follows רבי יהודה, and the reason is that the פסוק places a positive command after the prohibition. Without that, a person would get lashes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from Step 12. The leftover משנה may not be about 'no action' at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two possible reasons for no lashes in the leftover case. רבי יעקב's reason is that there was no action. רבי יהודה's reason is that this is a לאו הניתק לעשה, a prohibition fixed by a following positive command. If the משנה follows רבי יהודה, it does not show that a לאו שאין בו מעשה gets no lashes, so it cannot be רבי יוחנן's source.

keyTerms.meaning: But from where do we know?
A positive command placed after a prohibition (here: burning the leftover meat)
But if it were not so

steps.confusionAlert: Both רבי יעקב and רבי יהודה agree there are no lashes in the leftover case. They only disagree about WHY, and only רבי יעקב's reason helps רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatToRemember: The leftover-meat משנה cannot prove רבי יוחנן's rule, because it can be explained by רבי יהודה's reason (a לאו followed by an עשה) instead of 'no action'.

phrases.english: But from where do you know it is the view of Rabbi Yaakov,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר לָאו שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה אֵין לוֹקִין עָלָיו?
phrases.english: who says that for a prohibition with no action one does not receive lashes?
Perhaps it is the view of Rabbi Yehuda,
and the reason is that the verse comes
to place a positive command after the prohibition;
phrases.notes: The positive command is to burn whatever is left over, in the same פסוק (שמות 12:10).

phrases.english: but were it not for this, he would receive lashes!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in Step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the leftover-meat משנה as the source for רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'no lashes' ruling can be explained by רבי יהודה's reason (a לאו followed by an עשה), not by 'no action'.

steps.title: The ברייתא showing רבי יהודה and רבי יעקב argue about leftover פסח meat
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה exempts leftover פסח meat from lashes because an עשה follows the לאו. רבי יעקב says the reason is that it is a לאו שאין בו מעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: "Do not leave any of it until morning, and what is left of it until morning, burn in fire." The פסוק puts a positive command right after the prohibition to tell us that there are no lashes for it. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי יעקב says: That is not the reason. The reason is that it is a prohibition with no action, and there are no lashes for a prohibition with no action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source for what it just said in Step 13. The ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה has a different reason for no lashes on leftover פסח meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two תנאים agree there are no lashes for leaving over the פסח, but they disagree about why. For רבי יהודה it is because an עשה (burning) comes after the לאו. For רבי יעקב it is because nothing was done. So the משנה in פסחים fits רבי יהודה just as well, and it cannot prove the rule about a לאו שאין בו מעשה.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition followed by a positive command that fixes it. Here the burning follows the ban on leaving over meat.
A positive command, something you must do
They give lashes, the forty lashes

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the same ruling of no lashes can come from two different reasons. That is why one case cannot prove the general rule.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: "Do not leave any of it until morning,
and what is left of it until morning
you shall burn in fire".
The פסוק comes to place
a positive command after a prohibition,
to say that we do not give lashes for it;
these are the words of רבי יהודה.
רבי יעקב says:
That is not the reason,
rather, it is because it is
a prohibition that has no action,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָאו שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה אֵין לוֹקִים עָלָיו.
phrases.english: and for a prohibition that has no action we do not give lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the rejection in Step 13 by showing רבי יהודה's separate reason.
steps.raayaObject: The claim in Step 13 that רבי יהודה exempts leftover פסח meat only because an עשה follows the לאו
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on שמות 12:10 where רבי יהודה and רבי יעקב argue

steps.title: A different source: the משנה about swearing twice not to eat a loaf
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the משנה in פסחים and says רבי יוחנן found another unattributed משנה. In it, a person swears twice not to eat a certain loaf and then eats it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he found this unattributed משנה: "An oath that I will not eat this loaf," then "An oath that I will not eat it," and he ate it.
steps.whatsHappening: The proof from פסחים failed, so the גמרא answers the question of Step 11 with a new משנה. This line only sets up the case. The ruling and the proof come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here a person makes the same oath twice and then breaks it by eating. The second oath adds nothing new. The rest of the משנה, and how it points to no lashes for a לאו שאין בו מעשה, comes in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: An unattributed ruling, a משנה with no name attached

steps.confusionAlert: The quote stops in the middle of the משנה. Do not look for the ruling yet; the גמרא finishes the case in the next lines.

phrases.english: Rather, he found this unattributed משנה:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי יוחנן. The משנה is in this מסכת, later on (27b).

phrases.english: "An oath that I will not eat this loaf,"
"An oath that I will not eat it,"
and then he ate it —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from פסחים was rejected, the גמרא offers a new candidate for רבי יוחנן's source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which unattributed משנה רבי יוחנן relied on (asked in Step 11)
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה in שבועות about swearing twice not to eat a loaf and then eating it
